scope: Frozen readback of original 0ca272d observations and Host review; not execution or qualification of the r16 pagination candidate. No Host microbenchmark was executed.

construction_coverage.accounting_scope: construction intervals are nested in joined attacker worker CPU; never add them twice; shared public material setup is separate

caveats: All phase clocks are observer-local; CPU/wall nested spans cannot be added to their parents.
Host CPU sums actual invoking-thread intervals; it is not complete scoped-worker CPU.
Approximately 90-100 ms wall expansion is consistent with CPU scheduling/throttling; no scheduler trace proves each individual interval cause.
The 4-second 16-worker test and 30-second 24-process native campaign are distinct acceptance criteria.
No public-network saturation TPS or general production confirmation-security parameter follows from these controlled experiments.

original_native_campaign.verification_scope: Original job log plus retained campaign manifest; full 68 MB native ZIP was not downloaded in this review.

host_review.local_environment_limit: /sys and cgroupfs are absent in the local executor; actual full Host microbenchmark unavailable. A procfs-only draft was not compiled or executed.

fresh_checks_per_boundary: current invoking thread cgroup membership complete read
already_present_optimizations: stack buffers for common short values
duplicate native Host observation removed without removing progress boundaries

candidate_assessment.candidate: held parent directory plus fresh openat per limit
candidate_assessment.decision: bounded path-traversal optimization only; preserves fresh control-file opens and EOF reads when current path identity is checked before and after
candidate_assessment.cost: does not remove any of the five open/read-through-EOF/close operations; adds a second fresh parent-path metadata check

candidate_assessment.candidate: held proc root directory plus fresh thread-self/cgroup openat
candidate_assessment.decision: current thread is resolved when opened relative to /proc; never retain a /proc/thread-self directory opened by another thread
candidate_assessment.additional_obligation: must account for replacement of the current /proc mount/path; a pinned directory alone does not preserve current-path replacement detection

candidate_assessment.candidate: retained cgroup control FDs plus pread at offset zero
candidate_assessment.decision: do not implement as an equivalent optimization without additional proof and actual cgroupfs mutation controls
candidate_assessment.supported_positive: Reviewed Linux v6.18 seq_read_iter clears iterator/index and buffered count for offset zero; this avoids prior seq_file output reuse.
unresolved_or_non_equivalent: retained readable FD does not repeat current open permission/search/ACL checks
parent identity and CGROUP2_SUPER_MAGIC do not prove each current child path still names the retained file, including mount overlays
controller enable/disable can remove and recreate control files under a stable cgroup directory
complete multi-read/EOF operation requires external serialization if FD shared between threads; individual syscall locking is insufficient for the multi-call transaction
reviewed v6.18 implementation is not a proof covering every supported kernel

candidate_assessment.decision: no demonstrated material gain; operates on one FD and cannot merge reads across five control files; EOF/short-read/error semantics must remain

kernel_sources.finding: seq_read_iter resets index and count at offset zero; takes seq_file mutex per invocation.
kernfs_seq_start requires active node and returns ENODEV if inactive; uses per-open-file mutex.
control files use seq callbacks; cgroup_addrm_files can add/remove files on existing directory.
